confidence_notes: Hampi is a small tourist village with no standard price index, so the food and drink figures are bounded estimates. I ran three web searches. One gave the RBA rate. One returned Hampi guide pages: an aggregator (TripBase) with rough USD figures, a traveller blog quoting beer at about ₹180, and older local guides with rupee meal prices. One returned Bangalore crowdsourced cost-of-living data. The sources disagree: the TripBase coffee figure is about $1, while a local article quotes tea and coffee at ₹10-20. Beer is not always on menus in Hampi, and pricing is seasonal, with off-season lows from about April to September. Cocktail and wine are set from the beer price: cocktail about 1.8x beer, and a glass of wine about the same as a cocktail. Wine is rare and imported-priced in Hampi. Accommodation anchors are holistic model estimates from general knowledge and were not searched or checked against live listings. Registered hostels are few, and the nearest formal 3-star stock is mostly in Hospet or in resorts nearby.
comparable_city_reasoning: Used Hampi-specific guide figures, adjusted against Bangalore and general Karnataka and India backpacker-town prices. Hampi's tourist-hub markup is applied to the cheap local baseline, and the low-season July pricing window is taken into account.
